forces: Woodwinds, percussion, piano, harps, celesta and divided strings; no brass
performers: Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London; Artur Rodzinski, conductor
question: How does a movement without brass build such powerful climaxes—and make its quietest lines feel exposed?
intro: With the brass silent, the Largo redistributes the orchestra’s weight among divided strings, exposed woodwinds and a few sharply chosen keyboard and percussion colours. Rodzinski’s transfer contains two large waves of intensity separated by a much more fragile middle region.

sections.label: Divided-string opening
sections.mNote: Multiple string lines create an inward, layered opening.

sections.label: Flutes and harp · approximate
sections.mNote: A lighter contrast reduces the instrumental field.

sections.label: First broad crest
sections.mNote: The texture expands into the first measured climax.

sections.label: Exposed wind lines
sections.mNote: Solo lines emerge over much quieter string support.

sections.label: Renewed accumulation
sections.mNote: A second wave adds sharper attacks and greater density.

sections.label: Muted aftermath
sections.mNote: String colour and weight change after the second wave.

sections.label: Closing colours · approximate
sections.mNote: Harp and celesta bring the movement towards stillness.

cues.title: Strings divided more finely
cues.text: The score divides the violins into three groups, the violas into two and the cellos into two, alongside the basses. Listen for lines entering and sustaining independently: this is not simply a melody above one undifferentiated string cushion.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 85, rehearsal 75: eight string staves, with the third violin group initiating the line. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the opening remains restrained, around −20 to −17 dB over its first minute. The division is score-documented, not inferred from the audio analyser.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Growth inside the texture
cues.text: The opening grows without an abrupt change of instrumental family. Try following one sustained line while another moves: the sense of expansion can come from overlapping phrases as well as from a louder dynamic.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 85–87, layered divided strings. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: relative levels rise gradually through the first minute rather than showing an immediate tutti jump. Placement is within the opening region, not aligned to a particular entry.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Reception was not unanimous
cues.text: The premiere won extraordinary applause, but contemporary criticism was not uniformly celebratory. The publisher’s documentary account preserves objections to the symphony’s suffering and to the finale’s emotional character. Public success did not erase disagreement about what this music expressed.
cues.evidence: DSCH Publishers, work history and reception documents, including Alexander Ostretsov and Israel Nestyev: https://shostakovich-en.ru/140en . This concerns the symphony’s documented reception, not a claim that the Largo depicts a particular event.
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: A higher string horizon
cues.text: The opening string span reaches into a higher, more projecting register. Hear that change of register separately from the change in volume: the line can feel more exposed even while other strings continue to support it.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 87, rehearsal 78, high first-violin phrase with sustained lower lines. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: local level rises from about −17 dB at 1:20 to −13.5 at 1:35–1:40, followed by a continuing string span. The cue is deliberately passage-level.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Flute against a plucked sound
cues.text: The flutes and harp offer a different kind of continuity: a wind line can sustain while the harp’s sound begins to decay as soon as it is plucked. Listen to that contrast in the lighter passage after the opening strings.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 88, rehearsals 79–80: flute solo and harp, then a second flute; strings rest initially. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 2:34, with lower levels from 2:35 through the following quiet span. Exact first flute note is not aligned.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The quiet region starts to move
cues.text: The lighter span does not remain motionless. Its level begins to gather again, preparing the first broad wave. Follow the growth across phrases instead of treating the next loud moment as an isolated outburst.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: level rises from −20.9 dB at 3:15 to −17.4 at 3:20, −13.2 at 3:45 and −9.4 at 3:55.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: A crest without brass
cues.text: The first broad climax depends on strings and woodwinds rather than trumpets or trombones. Its force comes from intensifying and combining the available lines, not from adding the brass family held out of this movement.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 89–92, including woodwind-supported string expansion and timpani; brass has no part in the Largo. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: strong boundary at 3:54 and rising levels through 4:30.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The beginning of side two
cues.text: The Largo opens the LP’s second side, followed by the finale. Its label gives matrix XTV 22721. The digital track removes the need to turn the record, but the original carrier still helps identify exactly which performance is being heard.
cues.evidence: Original Westminster WN 18001 side-two label, PDF p. 4: https://archive.org/download/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony.pdf . No take or stamper suffix is inferred from the faint runout.
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: An oboe in the clearing
cues.text: After the first wave, the score exposes an oboe line above a quiet string tremolo. Listen for the difference between the solo’s shaped breath and the more continuous, trembling background.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 92, rehearsals 83–84: quieter string texture and oboe solo. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: strong boundary at 5:04, falling to −23.0 dB at 5:10 and −24.8 at 5:15. The timestamp marks the solo region approximately.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A long exposed middle
cues.text: The quiet after the climax is substantial, not a brief intake of breath. Let small inflections count: the recording remains at this reduced scale long enough for a single wind line to define the foreground.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: five-second levels from roughly 5:20 to 6:50 remain mostly between −23 and −28 dB. Wind-solo context is documented in https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 92–94.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: The solo colour is not fixed
cues.text: The middle span passes its exposed line between woodwind colours, including clarinet and flute. Follow the continuity of the phrase across those changes rather than assuming every new instrument introduces a new theme.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 94, clarinet/flute writing and rehearsal 86, over divided string tremolo. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: this cue lies in the extended low-level middle region; no exact clarinet-to-flute handoff is asserted at 6:40.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A small rise subsides
cues.text: A local increase in sound does not yet become the next large climax. Hear how the movement can gather briefly, pull back, and preserve its larger destination for later.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: level rises to −19.2 dB at 6:55 and −19.0 at 7:00, then returns to approximately −24 to −26 through much of 7:10–7:40.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: The next wave is assembling
cues.text: The wind-and-string texture begins to thicken again. The second large wave will not simply copy the first: listen for the harder attacks that enter as the sound accumulates.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 96–98, wind/string crescendo leading to piano and xylophone at rehearsal 89. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: levels around −20 to −21 dB before 8:20 give way to a sharp rise beginning at 8:20.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Piano and xylophone sharpen it
cues.text: Piano and xylophone reinforce the second wave with attacks that a sustained string line cannot make in the same way. The Largo’s intensity is being redistributed again, still without brass.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 98–99, rehearsal 89: piano and xylophone join winds and strings; timpani rests on the inspected page. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: strong boundaries at 8:40 and 8:54; levels around −6 dB at 8:40–8:50. This is a regional entry attribution.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Brightness at the crest
cues.text: This second wave is not only louder than the quiet middle; its sound is markedly brighter. Separate the high, active surface from the broader weight underneath it.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: relative level reaches −4.5 dB at 9:05; spectral-centroid windows around 9:10–9:25 rise to roughly 2.9–3.0 kHz. Brightness is an audio descriptor, not proof of one instrument.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: Which score did they use?
cues.text: The exact performing edition is not identified. The publisher documents differences among lifetime editions, especially the 1961 score, and uncertainty about authorization of some changes. The historical score supports this guide’s instrumentation; it does not prove every detail of Rodzinski’s conducting materials.
cues.evidence: DSCH Publishers, New Collected Works volume 5 editorial account: https://shostakovich-en.ru/272en . The inspected historical score is Muzgiz plate M. 16313 Г: https://imslp.org/wiki/Symphony_No.5%2C_Op.47_%28Shostakovich%2C_Dmitry%29 . No modern-edition reading is imposed on this recording.
cues.how: Documented fact.

cues.title: One more wave within the wave
cues.text: The second climax leaves behind further surges before the decisive withdrawal. Listen across them as one extended region: the music needs more than a single accent to discharge its accumulated weight.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: after the 9:05 peak, levels remain often around −9 to −12 dB, with another rise to −6.6 at 10:40; they fall to −22.6 at 11:00.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: Muted strings after the weight
cues.text: The score returns to a much quieter string sound, now explicitly muted. The change is not only a lower volume: the softened attack and colour make the aftermath different from the preceding exposed, forceful writing.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 105, rehearsals 92–93: withdrawal followed by muted strings marked pp. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the fall near 11:00 is followed by levels around −23 to −26 through 11:15. Passage placement is approximate.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A last modest swelling
cues.text: Even this reduced ending contains a small rise and fall. Follow it without expecting another central climax; the scale of the remaining gestures has changed.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: a local rise reaches −16.1 dB at 12:00, then falls to −27.5 at 12:10. Earlier boundaries at 11:44 and 11:56 mark activity within the quiet aftermath, not a new large climax.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

cues.title: Harp beside a single violin
cues.text: In the closing pages, harp and a solo line from the second violins emerge from the muted string field. Listen for the spare relation between a plucked attack and a sustained bowed sound.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 106–107, rehearsal 94 and following: harp line with second-violin solo and reduced strings. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the 12:15–13:10 region remains largely around −20 to −27 dB. No exact rehearsal-94 timestamp is asserted.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Celesta and harp harmonics
cues.text: The final page adds celesta and harp harmonics to the very quiet string world. Their small bright attacks are not a new climax; they change the quality of the stillness.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 108, rehearsal 96: celesta, harp harmonics and high string harmonics. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: levels around 13:15–13:40 remain near −27 to −29 dB. Cue identifies the closing-page region approximately.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Leave room for the decay
cues.text: The final sound is allowed to subside. Keep listening to the difference between the dying musical resonance and the constant residue of an LP transfer; neither should be mistaken for another written instrumental entry.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: −27.7 dB at 14:00, −29.3 at 14:05; decoded duration 848.3 seconds. The final-note release and noise floor have not been separately aligned.
cues.how: Located by measuring this recording.

transitions.title: Strings give way to a lighter pair
transitions.how: The opening string field releases its hold. Flute and harp establish a much more transparent relation between sustained melody and decaying accompaniment; a second flute subsequently joins. The timestamp is a regional anchor for the change, not a first-note claim.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, p. 88, rehearsals 79–80. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 2:34 and level withdrawal during 2:35–2:45.

transitions.title: The light texture gathers weight
transitions.how: Strings and woodwinds expand the lighter texture into the first broad crest. The join is cumulative: more weight and sustained pressure arrive across a span, rather than through a new brass entrance.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 89–92. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 3:54 and rise from −16.6 at 3:40 towards −7.7 at 4:00.

transitions.title: A broad wave leaves an exposed line
transitions.how: The first climax recedes and a solo woodwind line becomes exposed above quiet string tremolo. Reduced weight and a change of foreground, not a complete silence, define the new region.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, p. 92, rehearsals 83–84. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: strong boundary at 5:04; level reaches −24.8 dB at 5:15.

transitions.title: Sharper attacks join the growing texture
transitions.how: The quiet wind-and-string region accumulates weight again. Piano and xylophone add sharp attacks in the ensuing crest, giving this wave a different surface from the first one. The join marker precedes that full reinforcement.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 96–99, culminating at rehearsal 89. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 8:20 followed by strong changes at 8:40 and 8:54.

transitions.title: Weight withdraws into muted strings
transitions.how: The prolonged second wave loses its mass, leaving muted strings at a much lower level. The score changes tone colour as well as dynamic: this is a new degree of exposure, not merely the same climax played more softly.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, p. 105, rehearsals 92–93. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: −6.6 dB at 10:40 falls to −22.6 at 11:00 and −26.1 at 11:15.

transitions.title: The ending pares its colours down
transitions.how: Harp and a single violin line emerge from the muted string field; celesta and harmonics belong to the later closing page. The coda marker groups this final thinning, without pretending to locate the exact first harp or celesta note.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 106–108, rehearsals 94–96. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: reduced late region after the local 12:00 rise, continuing to 14:08.3.

source.title: Symphony No. 5 — Muzgiz M. 16313 Г, historical full score
source.locator: Printed pp. 85–108; PDF pp. 87–110. Brass absent. Three violin groups cannot map literally onto the diagram’s two violin IDs: violins-1/violins-2 jointly represent those groups. Score is public domain in Taiwan, not cleared for EU/US republication; exact performing edition unknown. Selected approximate passage snapshots use cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-largo.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony; not an exhaustive instrument-on/off transcript.

timeline.note: The third violin group initiates the opening, p. 85; its line is represented by violins-2. Lower-string entries follow within the opening passage.
High first-violin line and sustained divided strings, p. 87; broad opening-span placement.
Flute/harp contrast, p. 88/rehearsals 79–80; one flute, then two, with strings initially resting.
First expansion, pp. 89–92; selected active groups in the broad crest, not an exhaustive simultaneous chord inventory.
Oboe over high-string tremolo, p. 92/rehearsal 84; approximately after the 5:04 withdrawal.
Successive clarinet and flute solos over divided strings, p. 94; snapshot covers their passage, not a precisely timed duet.
Second climax, pp. 98–99/rehearsal 89: xylophone represented by percussion; timpani rests on this inspected page. Timing is regional.
Repeated clarinet figures above strongly projected cello material, pp. 100–102/rehearsals 90–91; selected layers in the extended second wave.
Muted string aftermath, p. 105/rehearsal 93; approximately after the 11:00 measured withdrawal.
Harp and second-violin solo with reduced string support, pp. 106–107/rehearsal 94; successive entries grouped into a passage snapshot.
Closing page, p. 108/rehearsal 96: celesta, harp harmonics and string harmonics, followed by the final string sonority. Not an exact celesta entry timestamp.

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London (orchestra), Artur Rodzinski (conductor)
fields.note: Original sleeve and labels establish the displayed credit. Later Westminster reissue documentation and the publisher’s discography identify the orchestra as the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. That cross-identification is not substituted silently for the original label credit; individual players and soloists are not established.

fields.label: Work version
fields.note: The work and movement are identified, but the exact performing edition is not. The historical score supports broad orchestration and formal observations, not a claim of bar-exact agreement with Rodzinski’s materials. The movement is the entire supplied source track; no local audio edit is made. The set’s finale has a separately disclosed reported cut.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: CiNii’s record for Westminster MVCW-18008 explicitly gives this range; the publisher independently lists the Rodzinski/Royal Philharmonic recording as 1954. Applying those reissue data to this differently credited LP is an inference. No original session ledger or precise movement-by-movement day has been located. 1956 is the selected LP’s publication year, not an invented session date.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: Venue transcribed exactly from the reissue catalogue record. The original LP does not supply a venue. Its linkage to the selected LP is the same qualified inference as the session-date attribution; no more specific hall name is invented.

fields.label: Label
fields.note: Original sleeve and labels; commercially issued Vinyl LP, Made in U.S.A. Sleeve ©1956 Westminster Recording Sales Corp.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.note: Both forms are visually present on the source object. These identify the selected 1956 issue, not an asserted first edition worldwide. The publisher lists an earlier 1955 Nixa issue of the attributed 1954 performance.

fields.note: Label matrix is legible in the scan. Side 1 contains Moderato/Allegretto; side 2 contains Largo/Allegro non troppo. Take numbers and faint runout/stamper suffixes are unknown and are not guessed.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Not cleared as public domain in the EU or US; composition rights remain separate from the historic recording basis
fields.note: Shostakovich died in 1975. The ordinary EU life-plus-70 calculation runs through 2045; this is not a global clearance or a statement of a US expiry date. IMSLP identifies the work as non-public-domain in the EU and US. The inspected score is territorially hosted as public domain in Taiwan and is cited, not republished. No composition licence is asserted.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: Rule 3: territorial EU historic-recording basis; commercial circulation documented by December 1955, selected LP issue dated 1956
fields.note: The original Westminster sleeve/labels and album metadata establish the selected 1956 WN 18001/XWN 18001 issue. A visually inspected High Fidelity review, December 1955, p. 80, already names this London orchestra, Rodzinski, his second recording of the Fifth and Westminster catalogue 18001; the review prints SWN 18001 and erroneously calls the symphony D major, so those details are not silently normalized. The publisher also lists Nixa WLP 20004 in 1955. First lawful publication anywhere before 1963 is the rule; no EU-first-release claim is required or made. source.rights.published 1956 remains a conservative upper bound tied to the selected physical issue, not a first-release date. Even using 1956, the ordinary 50-year recording term had expired before the 2013 extension. US sound-recording status is not established. Complete item metadata, original side-transfer provenance and scans disclose no Creative Commons non-commercial condition or separate upstream digital source. This is not a worldwide public-domain or composition-rights clearance.

sources.title: Westminster WN 18001 / XWN 18001 — original sleeve and labels
sources.locator: Four-page scan visually inspected. PDF p. 2: XWN 18001, ©1956 Westminster Recording Sales Corp., Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London/Artur Rodzinski, Peter Hugh Reed notes, tape recording by Panorthophonic technique and RIAA mastering. P. 3: WN 18001, side 1, XTV 22720. P. 4: WN 18001, side 2, XTV 22721; Made in U.S.A. Faint runout suffixes are not transcribed.

sources.title: Internet Archive — disc and track metadata
sources.locator: Album dated 1956; side 1 tracks Moderato/Allegretto, side 2 tracks Largo/Allegro Non Troppo. The four selected files are tracks from this source LP, not alternative performances.

sources.title: CiNii Books — Westminster MVCW-18008, Symphony No. 5
sources.locator: 1997 CD catalogue record, Royal Philharmonic Orchestra/Artur Rodzinski. Note: Recorded October 2 to 14, 1954, Walthamstow Hall, London. These are reissue-session data; the link to the differently named original LP orchestra is inferential, not a session ledger reproduced on the LP.

sources.title: DSCH Publishers — Symphony No. 5, Op. 47: history and discography
sources.locator: Composition 1937; premiere 21 November 1937, Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra/Mravinsky; first score publication 1939; contemporary reception documents; introduction to the 1956 score. Discography lists Rodzinski/Royal Philharmonic, 1954, Nixa WLP 20004, mono, 1955. The latter is an earlier-publication lead, not needed to establish the documented 1956 upper bound for the selected LP.

sources.title: DSCH Publishers — New Collected Works, volume 5 editorial account
sources.locator: Instrumentation and historical score editions (1939, 1947, 1956, 1961); manuscript not located; uncertainty about authorial sanction for some 1961 changes. Does not identify Rodzinski’s performing edition.

sources.title: IMSLP — Symphony No. 5, Op. 47, historical full-score catalogue
sources.locator: Historical full score, item 1014274, Muzgiz plate M. 16313 Г, circa 1939, Edition Musicus reprint. PML-Asia territorial public-domain hosting; the catalogue marks the work non-public-domain in Canada, the US and the EU. No score file is republished by this package.

sources.title: Symphony No. 5 — inspected historical full score
sources.locator: Printed pp. 85–108; PDF pp. 87–110. 170-page PDF; printed pages are PDF page minus two. Relevant pages were visually inspected for orchestration. This source is a historical score witness, not proof of the exact performing edition or a bar-aligned transcript of the cut finale.

sources.title: Niek Nelissen — Artur Rodzinski, Complete Westminster Recordings
sources.locator: OpusKlassiek, August 2026, Eloquence 484 8489 review. Early paragraph specifies a 37-bar cut in the 1942 Fifth finale; the later Westminster paragraph explicitly states that Rodzinski made the same cut. This supports a reported version difference, not the exact omitted bars or the splice time in this transfer.

sources.title: Museum collection — Pravda, “Muddle Instead of Music,” 28 January 1936
sources.locator: Catalogue of the surviving printed clipping of “Сумбур вместо музыки,” Pravda, 28 January 1936, inventory КП 317996/1315. Establishes the dated public attack, not a decoded political programme for individual notes.

sources.title: Harlow Robinson — Boston Symphony Orchestra work note
sources.locator: Used for Shostakovich’s dates (1906–1975) and the first American performance, Rodzinski/NBC Symphony broadcast, 9 April 1938. The note’s broader interpretive narrative is not treated as proof of private intentions.

sources.title: Testimony — publication and authenticity controversy
sources.locator: 1979 publication by Solomon Volkov, and summary/bibliography of the authenticity dispute, including Laurel Fay. Used only to identify the disputed status of the memoir claim, not as authentication of a Shostakovich quotation.

sources.title: Alex Ross — Unauthorized
sources.locator: The New Yorker, 30 August 2004 / 6 September print issue. Reports Testimony’s 1979 publication, Laurel Fay’s documentary challenge and the continuing distinction between corroborated anecdotes and authenticated authorship. Used as independent evidence of the controversy, not as a settled verdict on every memoir statement or on the finale’s meaning.

sources.title: Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright and related-rights terms
sources.locator: Article 1(1), ordinary life-plus-70 author term; Article 3, former 50-year phonogram/performer terms; Article 8, calculation from the following January; recital 17, relevant acts count regardless of country.

sources.title: Decca Eloquence — Artur Rodzinski, Complete Westminster Recordings
sources.locator: Label’s catalogue 4848489, CD 16: Shostakovich Symphony No. 5, Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. Quotes a High Fidelity review dated December 1955; that original review was subsequently located and visually inspected (source contemporary-review). The exact session ledger remains unavailable; inferred session fields are retained.

sources.title: High Fidelity — Shostakovich Fifth, Westminster 18001, December 1955
sources.locator: Printed p. 80, PDF p. 82, first column, review signed A. F.; original scan visually inspected, with December 1955 footer confirmed on printed p. 67/PDF p. 69. Names Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London/Artur Rodzinski and explicitly identifies his second recording. Catalogue is printed SWN 18001, price $4.98 (or $3.98); work key is misprinted D major. Evidence of circulation by December 1955, not an exact first-release day.

sources.title: Directive 2011/77/EU — sound-recording term extension
sources.locator: Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): the extension applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. A recording lawfully published by 1956 had exhausted the ordinary 50-year term before that extension.

composer.epithet: Fifteen symphonies and fifteen quartets turn marches, fugues and a four-note signature into arguments about public ceremony and individual memory.
facts: Petrograd Conservatory from 1919: piano with Leonid Nikolayev, composition with Maximilian Steinberg
Leningrad Conservatory from 1937; Moscow Conservatory from 1943; dismissed from both in 1948
DSCH = D–E♭–C–B, using German note names
Fifteen symphonies · fifteen string quartets · six concertos · operas, songs and film scores
composer.background:
Dmitri Shostakovich was born in St Petersburg in 1906, the son of an engineer and a pianist. His mother, Sofiya, gave him his first piano lessons; in 1919 he entered the Petrograd Conservatory, where Leonid Nikolayev taught him piano and Maximilian Steinberg composition. The director, Alexander Glazunov, supported the young musician through the shortages following revolution and civil war. His father’s death in 1922 worsened the family’s finances, and Shostakovich earned money accompanying silent films. He graduated in piano in 1923 and composition in 1925: the graduation score was his First Symphony, written before his nineteenth birthday.

Nikolai Malko conducted its première in Leningrad on 12 May 1926. The orchestra includes a piano, whose abrupt interventions contribute to the symphonic argument. Clarinet, bassoon and trumpet exchange short phrases; a waltz can become a march without a change of personnel. International performances followed. Shostakovich still considered a performing career and received an honourable mention at the first Warsaw Chopin Competition in 1927. Thereafter his public piano appearances increasingly centred on his own works, including the concertos, chamber music and songs.
